knowledge:
- key_parameters: measurements=The input data, which can be a matrix, data.frame, DataFrame, MultiAssayExperiment, or list of data.frames ;; classes/outcome=The target variable, which can be a factor of class labels, a column name character, a Surv object, or a character vector of time/censoring column names ;; classifier=Specifies the classification algorithm (e.g., "SVM", "naiveBayes", "randomForest") ;; nFolds and nRepeats=Control the cross-validation structure (number of folds and repeats) ;; multiViewMethod=Used for integrating multiple data sources (e.g., "merge") ;; tuneParams=A named list passed to TrainParams or SelectParams to specify parameter tuning grids and the optimization metric (via "performanceType") ;; parallelParams=Controls parallel processing backend (e.g., SnowParam or MulticoreParam with RNGseed)
- alternatives: caret=Compared in the documentation; caret lacks direct support for MultiAssayExperiment, ranking/selection plots, class distribution plots, and sample-wise error heatmaps ;; MLInterfaces, MCRestimate, CMA=Other classification frameworks compared in the documentation, which lack various features like parallel execution on any OS, parameter tuning, or specialized plots that ClassifyR provides
- when_to_use: Use ClassifyR when performing cross-validated classification, survival analysis, multi-omics (multi-view) data integration, and comparing different feature selection/classification algorithms on high-dimensional biological data (e.g., transcriptomics, genomics).
- pitfalls: Failing to set the random number seed (set.seed or RNGseed in parallel backends) before cross-validation, which compromises reproducibility ;; Using the standard seed argument for parallel processes (it does not work; RNGseed must be set in the parallel backend like SnowParam or MulticoreParam) ;; Feature names must match across datasets when cross-validating selected features on a different dataset

workflows.name: quick_start_cross_validation
workflows.intent: Perform a quick cross-validated classification on a single dataset using a specified classifier and plot the performance.
input: measurements (matrix or data.frame of numeric features)
workflows.stages: 1. Set random seed for reproducibility ;; 2. Run cross-validation using crossValidate ;; 3. Plot performance using performancePlot
workflows.code:
library(ClassifyR)
data(asthma) # Contains measurements and classes variables.
measurements[1:5, 1:5]
head(classes)
set.seed(9500)
result <- crossValidate(measurements, classes, classifier = "SVM",
                        nFolds = 5, nRepeats = 2, nCores = 1)
performancePlot(result)

workflows.name: multi_view_integration
workflows.intent: Integrate data from multiple sources/assays into a single classification model using crossValidate.
input: measurementsDF (DataFrame with column metadata mcols) or measurementsList (list of data.frames)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare multi-view data (either as a DataFrame with assay metadata or as a named list of data.frames) ;; 2. Run cross-validation with multiViewMethod = "merge" ;; 3. Plot performance grouped by assay
workflows.code:
measurementsDF <- DataFrame(measurements)
mcols(measurementsDF) <- data.frame(
  assay = rep(c("assay_1", "assay_2"), times = c(10, 1990)),
  feature = colnames(measurementsDF)
)

result <- crossValidate(measurementsDF, classes, classifier = "SVM", nFolds = 5,
                        nRepeats = 3, multiViewMethod = "merge")

performancePlot(result, characteristicsList = list(x = "Assay Name"))

# Assigns first 10 variables to dataset_1, and the rest to dataset_2
measurementsList <- list(
  (measurements |> as.data.frame())[1:10],
  (measurements |> as.data.frame())[11:2000]
)
names(measurementsList) <- c("assay_1", "assay_2")

result <- crossValidate(measurementsList, classes, classifier = "SVM", nFolds = 5,
                        nRepeats = 3, multiViewMethod = "merge")

performancePlot(result, characteristicsList = list(x = "Assay Name"))

workflows.name: advanced_modelling_and_evaluation
workflows.intent: Perform fine-grained cross-validation using runTests with custom parameters, calculate performance metrics, and generate diagnostic plots.
input: measurements (matrix or data.frame of numeric features)
workflows.stages: 1. Define cross-validation parameters using CrossValParams ;; 2. Run default differential means (DM) model using runTests ;; 3. Plot top selected features using plotFeatureClasses ;; 4. Calculate performance metrics using calcCVperformance ;; 5. Define and run a custom differential distribution (DD) model using ModellingParams ;; 6. Compare models using samplesMetricMap, performancePlot, rankingPlot, and ROCplot
workflows.code:
crossValParams <- CrossValParams(permutations = 5)
DMresults <- runTests(measurements, classes, crossValParams, verbose = 1)
library(grid)
selectionPercentages <- distribution(DMresults, plot = FALSE)
head(selectionPercentages)
sortedPercentages <- head(selectionPercentages[order(selectionPercentages, decreasing = TRUE)])
head(sortedPercentages)
mostChosen <- sortedPercentages[1]
bestGenePlot <- plotFeatureClasses(measurements, classes, names(mostChosen), dotBinWidth = 0.1,
                                   xAxisLabel = "Normalised Expression")
grid.draw(bestGenePlot[[1]])
DMresults <- calcCVperformance(DMresults)
DMresults
performance(DMresults)
modellingParamsDD <- ModellingParams(selectParams = SelectParams("KL"),
                                     trainParams = TrainParams("naiveBayes"),
                                     predictParams = NULL)
DDresults <- runTests(measurements, classes, crossValParams, modellingParamsDD, verbose = 1)
DDresults
resultsList <- list(Abundance = DMresults, Distribution = DDresults)
samplesMetricMap(resultsList, showXtickLabels = FALSE)
performancePlot(resultsList)
rankingPlot(DDresults, topRanked = 1:100, xLabelPositions = c(1, seq(10, 100, 10)))
ROCplot(resultsList, fontSizes = c(24, 12, 12, 12, 12))

workflows.name: parameter_tuning
workflows.intent: Optimize model hyperparameters (e.g., SVM cost) during cross-validation and extract the tuned parameters.
input: measurements (matrix or data.frame of numeric features)
workflows.stages: 1. Define a tuning grid list ;; 2. Set up CrossValParams with a tuning mode ;; 3. Define ModellingParams with TrainParams containing the tuning list ;; 4. Run cross-validation using runTests ;; 5. Extract and inspect tuned parameters using tunedParameters
workflows.code:
tuneList <- list(cost = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10))
crossValParams <- CrossValParams(permutations = 5, tuneMode = "Resubstitution")
SVMparams <- ModellingParams(trainParams = TrainParams("SVM", kernel = "linear", tuneParams = tuneList),
                             predictParams = PredictParams("SVM"))
SVMresults <- runTests(measurements, classes, crossValParams, SVMparams)
length(tunedParameters(SVMresults))
tunedParameters(SVMresults)[1:5]
